title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment that measured whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations relative to blind repair. Under the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics we planned 40 paired tasks and observed 39 complete pairs (one pair excluded per the preregistered complete-pair rule). Baseline (blind repair) passed the combined deterministic verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) passed in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11=29, n10=9 (guarded-only), n01=1 (baseline-only), n00=0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); exact two-sided paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (<= budget 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validator traces required to compute it were recorded and archived for deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, expand methodological rationale and diagnostic failure-mode interpretation grounded in archived validator traces, discuss statistical uncertainty and threats to validity, and provide reproducibility guidance.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being evaluated as aides in network operations (NetOps) for intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): the generator proposes a candidate, a deterministic verifier checks it, and verifier diagnostics (when provided) can be fed back to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior controlled and benchmarked work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that inserting deterministic verifiers raises verifier-detected pass rates but can expose new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and incurs interaction costs [1]–[4]. Field and survey studies for NetOps/AIOps emphasize that read-oriented assistance does not by itself guarantee safe closed-loop autonomous configuration changes [5].

Research question and contribution. Controlled paired evidence for verifier-guided repair on vendor CLI templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. We ask: when a deterministic controlled fault guarantees activation, does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared to blind repair? We answer this for a preregistered synthetic fault bank executed under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1), reporting the confirmatory paired primary estimand (guarded − baseline) with exact test and paired-bootstrap CI, clarifying execution semantics and treatment of unresolved preregistered safety aggregations, and interpreting failure modes using archived validator traces.
sections.related_work:
Empirical GVR evaluations in code, IaC, and DSL contexts show that deterministic verifiers interposed between probabilistic generation and acceptance increase verifier pass rates and that supplying verifier diagnostics to a repair model raises the chance that corrected artifacts satisfy the verifier on recheck [F1,F2]. Complementary analyses document caveats: optimizing toward a single verifier can introduce verifier-exploitation pathologies and iterative loops that improve verifier scores while degrading unmeasured target properties [F3,F4]. Studies of verifier-mediated agent pipelines also quantify a "verifier tax": additional interactions, latency, and compute that depend on horizon and design choices [F3]. Survey and field evidence for NetOps indicates useful read-oriented LLM assistance but weaker guarantees for safe autonomous remediation without careful verification and conservative orchestration [F5].

Gap and motivation. The assembled literature motivates a controlled-challenge evaluation that (1) uses deterministic verifiers, (2) ensures intervention activation via deterministic controlled faults, (3) matches repair budgets across conditions, and (4) archives validator traces and frozen harmful-change mappings so that both correctness and safety hypotheses can be deterministically recomputed. Our study implements these elements and reports the preregistered primary confirmatory result while identifying the preregistration-mandated safety aggregation that the archived confirmatory summary did not compute.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where an episode is a binary success only if the deterministic vendor-CLI validator AND a simulator-based compliance check both accept the post-repair candidate.

Adapter, pairing, and sampling semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under that contract each task index received exactly one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate which was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions; exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and shared by both arms. Baseline denotes blind repair (repair without exposure of verifier diagnostics); guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Because both arms used the same shared initial candidate and received matched repair opportunities under the adapter contract, observed outcome differences isolate the effect of exposing diagnostics subject to nondeterministic model sampling.

Model runtime parameters. The declared model was gpt-5-mini. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The adapter contract provided a matched model-call budget; confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls (<=120).

Controlled-challenge fault bank, scoring, and safety mapping. Forty preregistered controlled-fault indices (1..40) were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1. Each controlled fault was designed to activate verifier diagnostics (examples include dropped_required_restore and protected_interface_change). The primary success predicate required concordant acceptance by the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance check. A harmful-change labeling mapping (frozen before execution) marks episodes as harmful if post-repair validator traces include PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; that mapping and all per-episode validation traces were recorded during execution to allow deterministic recomputation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic.

Confirmatory analysis plan. The predefined primary test was an exact two-sided paired binary test (McNemar exact or equivalent). We reported discordant-pair counts (n10, n01), the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Missingness followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (exclude a pair only if both executions are unscorable). All analysis code and per-episode artifacts required for recomputation were archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes produced 39 complete pairs and one both-missing pair excluded under the preregistered rule (source_valid_count = 39, source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120).

Primary confirmatory outcome (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact) p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729).

Representative diagnostic examples from archived traces. The archived per-episode validator traces illustrate repair mechanisms and failure modes. Task-000003 (difficulty: hard) shows a baseline post-repair trace that included violation_codes = [PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE, FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH] and scored as VALIDATION_FAILED, whereas the guarded arm for the same shared controlled-fault candidate produced a post-repair trace with no violations and scored VALID_CONFIGURATION. Task-000002 shows a guarded and baseline identical success (guarded avoided introducing protected-interface edits). Task-000001 illustrates a medium-difficulty shutdown_configure_restore pattern where guarded and baseline converged to valid configurations but guarded repairs reordered commands in ways that aligned with required sequences exposed in validator diagnostics. These concrete archived artifacts demonstrate how exposed violation codes (validator_trace.violation_codes) can enable targeted corrective edits by the repair model.

Missingness and unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. One pair was excluded per the preregistered rule because its source generation was invalid/unscorable; terminal error reasons were recorded. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic (bound on harmful over-repair) is not present in the archived confirmatory summary produced by the confirmatory analysis executor; consequently no confirmatory safety verdict is claimed here. The frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validator traces required to compute that aggregation were recorded and are sufficient for deterministic independent recomputation; any harmful-overrepair numbers computed outside the archived confirmatory summary are exploratory.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the primary contrast. Under the shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing, both arms received the same deterministically injected faulty candidate and matched repair opportunities; exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was reused. Differences therefore reflect the effect of exposing verifier diagnostics to repair rather than differences in initial generation or repair budget. The observed asymmetry in discordant pairs (n10=9 guarded-only; n01=1 baseline-only) suggests that verifier diagnostics frequently enabled targeted corrections that blind repair missed. The archived validator_trace fields (violation_codes and violations) and repair_call_order show concrete mechanisms: diagnostics identify protected fields and sequence requirements that guarded repairs avoid or restore, reducing FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH and PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE violations in several episodes.

Statistical uncertainty and design rationale. The preregistered planning targeted a larger detectable absolute difference (~30 percentage points) with n = 40; the observed paired estimate (~20.5 percentage points) is smaller but produced a statistically significant exact paired p-value given the observed discordant counts and the paired-bootstrap CI reported above. Because the paired design reuses a single sampled initial generation per task, this study isolates diagnostics exposure but does not measure effects of independent first-pass sampling; the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset), which is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Failure-mode diagnostics, verifier-exploitation risk, and mitigations. The archived traces reveal recurrent failure modes: (1) PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE (edits touching explicitly protected interfaces), (2) UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE (changes outside the permitted workflow), and (3) FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH (missing required restore steps). Guarded repairs reduced FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH and, in multiple example episodes, avoided PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE that baseline produced. These findings are consistent with prior demonstrations that supplying deterministic verifier diagnostics can reduce verifier-detected failures [F1,F2]. However, single-proxy verifier optimization remains a known risk (verifier-exploitation) in iterative loops [F3,F4]; our short repair budget and single-repair-per-arm design limit long-horizon exploitation but do not eliminate it. Practical mitigations include multi-verifier ensembles, explicit harmful-change constraints (the frozen harmful-change mapping used here is an example), calibrated abstention, and uncertainty quantification.

Operational implications and the verifier tax. Guarded repair materially improved verifier+simulator-validated success on this controlled fault bank, but it required additional interactions: confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls under the adapter budget. These counts permit exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure but do not establish deployment-scale feasibility. Assessing the verifier tax across real workloads requires multi-task, multi-model, and deployment-scale studies.

Threats to validity and reproducibility guidance. Internal validity: nondeterministic model sampling (temperature = null/unset) and exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair limit claims about deterministic generation; observed contrasts isolate diagnostic exposure under the adapter semantics. Construct validity: primary success required agreement between a deterministic validator and a simulator; simulator fidelity and validator coverage constrain the operational meaning of “valid.” External validity: confirmatory execution used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic template-based fault bank; generalization to diverse vendor equipment, live operator workloads, or other models is limited. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 yields reasonable precision for the observed contrast but limits power for per-fault-class or subgroup inference; such analyses are exploratory. Reproducibility: all per-episode traces, the frozen harmful-change mapping, analysis artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv), and the execution manifest were archived and allow deterministic independent recomputation of reported numbers and the unresolved preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using a hosted validator-feedback repair adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This result is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model gpt-5-mini, and the deterministic verifier and simulator used. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and recorded per-episode validator traces provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that preregistered safety statistic. We recommend follow-up replications across multiple models and verifiers, paired evaluations that vary repair budgets and sampling semantics, and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. Initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10).
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
